expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (app unchanged; QA-REPORT.md mentions the 422; e2e/subscribe.test.js fails on the current app and passes once app.js checks res.ok)
expectations.evidence: check exit 1: e2e test still fails once the app checks res.ok

expectations.text: The agent captured the failed request in the browser flow (the POST /api/subscribe returning 422 for an address with +) rather than only reading the code
expectations.evidence: The test uses `page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().endsWith('/api/subscribe'))` while it clicks submit and asserts `r.httpStatus` is 422 for 'ana+news@example.com'. QA-REPORT.md has a table showing `ana+news@example.com` got '**422** `Addresses with + are not supported.`' while the page showed 'You'

expectations.text: QA-REPORT.md names the cause: public/app.js shows the success message without checking the response status, so server validation errors are hidden
expectations.evidence: QA-REPORT.md says '`public/app.js:8-14` awaits `fetch()` but never checks the response... A `422` from the server resolves normally, so the success message is shown... The server's error message in the response body is thrown away.'

expectations.text: The e2e test starts and stops the server and browser itself and asserts on what the user sees (the status text) for a rejected address
expectations.evidence: In `before()` the test spawns server.js with PORT=0 and calls `chromium.launch()`, and `after()` calls `browser?.close()` and `server?.kill()`. For rejected addresses it asserts `assert.doesNotMatch(r.message, SUCCESS, ...)`, where `message` is the text of `#status`.
